figures.title: Esophagus: CSTB immunohistochemistry
figures.caption: Esophagus tissue stained for cystatin B (CSTB). Brown: CSTB protein. Blue: cell nuclei (hematoxylin counterstain).
figures.alt: Microscope image of esophagus tissue with CSTB protein stained brown and cell nuclei stained blue.
figures.credit: Image from the Human Protein Atlas 25.1 (proteinatlas.org): Esophagus: CSTB immunohistochemistry, https://images.proteinatlas.org/47320/103193_B_4_1.jpg. CC BY 4.0.

figures.title: Esophagus
figures.caption: The upper esophageal sphincter controls the movement of food from the pharynx to the esophagus. The lower esophageal sphincter controls the movement of food from the esophagus to the stomach.
figures.alt: This diagram shows the esophagus, going from the mouth to the stomach. The upper and the lower esophageal sphincter are labeled.
figures.credit: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax. Figure “Esophagus”, section 23.3 The Mouth, Pharynx, and Esophagus. CC BY 4.0. Access for free at https://openstax.org/books/anatomy-and-physiology-2e/pages/1-introduction
